items.title: Which of the Four Conditions Actually Links Each Pair — and Why Never a Causal One

items.zh: 問：無明望行為幾種緣？答：望諸色行為增上緣，望無色行為三緣。謂等無間緣、所緣緣、增上緣。如是餘支為緣多少，應如此知。謂有色支望有色支，為一增上緣；望無色支為二緣，謂所緣緣及增上緣。若無色支望有色支，唯為一緣；望無色支為三緣；謂等無間緣、所緣緣、增上緣。
items.en: Question: In relation to formations, how many kinds of condition does ignorance provide? Answer: In relation to physical formations, a dominant condition alone; in relation to mental formations, three conditions — the immediately-preceding condition, the objective condition, and the dominant condition. Every other pair of links should be understood the same way: a physical link, in relation to a further physical link, provides a dominant condition alone; in relation to a mental link, two conditions — the objective and the dominant. A mental link, in relation to a physical link, provides only one condition; in relation to a further mental link, three — the immediately-preceding, the objective, and the dominant.

items.zh: 問：何故諸支相望無因緣耶？答：因緣者，自體種子緣所顯故。問：若諸支相望無因緣者，何故說言：依因果體性建立緣起耶？
items.en: Question: Why is there never a causal condition between any two links? Answer: A causal condition is, by its own nature, revealed only through a thing's own seed. Question: If there is never a causal condition between the links, then why is it said that dependent origination is established resting on the very nature of cause and result?

items.title: Resolving the Puzzle: Three Sub-Kinds of Dominant Condition Are What "Cause and Result" Actually Means

items.zh: 答：依增上緣所攝引發因、牽引因、生起因故，說名為因。問：幾支是引因所攝？答：從無明乃至受。問：幾支是生因所攝？答：從愛乃至有。問：幾支是生、引二因果所攝耶？答：於現法後法中，識等乃至受，於生、老死位所攝諸支。
items.en: Answer: It is on the basis of the inducing cause, the projecting cause, and the generating cause — all three included within the dominant condition — that dependent origination is spoken of in terms of cause. Question: Which links are included within the projecting cause? Answer: From ignorance through feeling. Question: Which links are included within the generating cause? Answer: From craving through becoming. Question: Which links are included among the results of the generating and projecting causes? Answer: In this present existence and the next, consciousness through feeling, and, at the stages of birth and old-age-and-death, the links belonging to them.

items.title: Why Ignorance, Not Wrong Attention, Opens the Chain — and Why Even Merit Still Depends on It

items.zh: 問：若說無明以不如理作意為因，何因緣故於緣起教中不先說耶？答：彼唯是不斷因故，非雜染因故。所以者何？非不愚者起此作意。依雜染因說緣起教。無明自性是染污，不如理作意自性非染污，故彼不能染污無明，然由無明力所染污。又生雜染業煩惱力之所熏發，業之初因謂初緣起。是故不說不如理作意。
items.en: Question: If ignorance is said to have unsound reasoning attention as its cause, why is that attention not taught first in the teaching of dependent origination? Answer: Unsound reasoning attention is merely a cause preventing ignorance's severance, not a cause of its defilement. It is never anyone but the already-deluded who gives rise to it in the first place. The teaching of dependent origination is given specifically in terms of the cause of defilement: ignorance is itself defiled by nature, while unsound reasoning attention is not defiled by nature — so it cannot itself defile ignorance, but is rather defiled by ignorance's own power. Further, the defilement of rebirth is brought about by the power of karma and affliction together, and the very first cause of karma is this same original link of dependent origination. This is why unsound reasoning attention is not spoken of first.

items.zh: 問：何故不說自體為自體緣耶？答：由彼自體若不得餘緣，於自體雜染不能增長，亦不損減，是故不說。問：何因緣故，福行、不動行由正簡擇功力而起，仍說用無明為緣耶？答：由不了達世俗苦因為緣，起非福行；由不了達勝義苦因為緣，生福及不動行；是故亦說彼以無明為緣。
items.en: Question: For what reason are meritorious karma and unmoving karma, which arise through the genuine effort of careful discernment, still said to have ignorance as their condition? Answer: Conditioned by failing to fathom the cause of conventional suffering, demeritorious karma arises; conditioned by failing to fathom the cause of ultimate suffering, meritorious and unmoving karma arise — and this is why these, too, are said to have ignorance as their condition.

items.title: Why This Link and Not an Equally Plausible Rival — Five More Sharp Questions Answered

items.zh: 問：如經中說：諸業以貪瞋癡為緣。何故此中唯說癡為緣耶？答：此中通說福、非福、不動業緣，貪瞋癡緣唯生非福業故。問：身業、語業思所發起，是則行亦緣行；何故但說無明緣行？答：依發起一切行緣而說故，及依生善、染污思緣而說故。
items.en: Question: The sūtras say karma is conditioned by craving, hatred, and delusion — why does this teaching name only delusion as the condition? Answer: This teaching covers meritorious, demeritorious, and unmoving karma alike, while craving, hatred, and delusion as condition produce only demeritorious karma. Question: Since bodily and verbal karma are themselves set in motion by intention, is not formations itself, in a sense, the condition for formations — why say only that ignorance conditions formations? Answer: This is stated in terms of what conditions every kind of formation, and in terms of what conditions both wholesome and defiled intention alike.

items.zh: 問：識亦以名色為緣，何故此中但說行為緣耶？答：行為識雜染緣，能引、能生後有果故。非如名色，但為所依、所緣，生起緣故。問：名色亦由大種所造及由觸生，何故但說識為緣耶？答：識能為彼新生因故。彼既生已，或正生時，大種及觸唯能與彼為建立因。
items.en: Question: Consciousness, too, is conditioned by name-and-form — why does this teaching name only formations as its condition? Answer: Formations condition consciousness's own defilement, capable of both projecting and generating a further existence's result — unlike name-and-form, which serves only as consciousness's basis and object, a mere condition for its arising. Question: Name-and-form, too, arises from the great elements and from contact — why name only consciousness as its condition? Answer: Consciousness alone is the cause of name-and-form's very arising; once name-and-form has arisen, or is in the process of arising, the great elements and contact serve only as its supporting, not its originating, cause.

items.zh: 問：如經中說：六界為緣得入母胎。何故此中唯說識界？答：若有識界，決定於母胎中精血、大種、腹穴無闕故。又識界勝故。又依一切生、一切有生時而說故。問：六處亦以飲食為緣，何故此中但說名色為緣耶？答：此中說名色是彼生因故。彼既生已，亦以飲食為任持因。
items.en: Question: The sūtras say the six elements together are the condition for entering the womb — why does this teaching name only the element of consciousness? Answer: Wherever the element of consciousness is present, the womb's blood and semen, the great elements, and the bodily cavity are all, without exception, already present as well. Further, the element of consciousness is simply the most decisive of the six. Further, this is stated in terms of what applies across every mode and every realm of birth. Question: The six sense-bases, too, are conditioned by food — why name only name-and-form as their condition? Answer: This teaching names name-and-form as their originating cause; once the bases have arisen, food then serves as the cause that merely sustains them.

blocks.text: Today's reading is technical and rewarding. It asks which of the four conditions connects each link to the next, and arrives at a surprising answer: never the causal condition. It then defends the order of the links against sharp objections, beginning with why ignorance, and not unsound attention, opens the chain.

Ignorance conditions bodily formations only as a dominant condition, and mental formations as three conditions: immediately preceding, object, and dominant. And so on through the links. But no link ever provides the **causal condition** for the next, because the causal condition "is revealed only through a thing's own seed". Venerable Miào Jìng: "A causal condition is a thing relative to itself, for example ignorance's seed producing manifest ignorance." Formations do not grow from the seed of ignorance; they grow from their own seeds.

When the resulting link is physical (as with old age and death), there is no object condition either, because matter does not cognise. Master Cháng Bǎi: "the form aggregate in old age and death cannot cognise an object."

If no link causes the next in the strict sense, why speak of the twelve links as cause and result? The answer: three kinds of cause, all included in the **dominant condition**: the inducing cause, the **projecting cause**, and the **generating cause** (Day 65). Venerable Miào Jìng, citing a sūtra: the projecting cause is the remote dominant condition; the generating cause, the near one.
This is a distinctly Yogācāra position. Each link has its own seed in the ālayavijñāna; the links influence one another, decisively, but do not produce one another.

subs.head: Why ignorance and not unsound attention?

blocks.text: Ignorance itself has a cause, unsound attention (Day 36). Why not begin the chain with that? Because unsound attention "is merely a cause preventing ignorance's severance, not a cause of its defilement". Master Cháng Bǎi: it obstructs the antidote, so ignorance is not cut. Venerable Miào Jìng states the principle: "only what is defiled is listed in the twelve links." Attention is not defiled by nature; it is neutral, and can be sound or unsound.

Meritorious and unmoving karma come from careful thought, not from confusion. Why say they are conditioned by ignorance? "Conditioned by failing to fathom the cause of conventional suffering, demeritorious karma arises; conditioned by failing to fathom the cause of ultimate suffering, meritorious and unmoving karma arise." Venerable Miào Jìng: "Only the noble know that worldly wealth and glory are suffering, and heavenly meditative states too; ordinary beings don't."

This is a crucial point for practice. Good karma done without understanding non-self still builds saṃsāra, a pleasanter part of it. Only wisdom produces the fourth kind of karma of Day 63, the kind that ends karma.

The treatise defends the order of each link against an equally plausible rival: why formations and not something else after ignorance, why consciousness after formations, and so on. Each answer turns on the same structure: projecting cause, projected result, generating cause, generated result.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, how many conditions does ignorance provide for formations?
options: for physical formations, the dominant condition alone; for mental formations, three — immediately-preceding, objective, dominant
quiz.why: "In relation to physical formations, a dominant condition alone; in relation to mental formations, three conditions — the immediately-preceding condition, the objective condition, and the dominant condition." Venerable Miào Jìng: bodily and verbal formations are physical, mental formation is not.

quiz.q: The text says links never provide a causal condition, since it is "revealed only through a thing's own seed." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain?
options: a causal condition is a thing relative to itself — ignorance's seed producing manifest ignorance
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "A causal condition is a thing relative to itself — e.g. ignorance's seed producing manifest ignorance." Master Cháng Bǎi: formations likewise come from formations' own seeds. So between different links there is no causal condition.

quiz.q: If the links share no causal condition, why speak of cause and result? What does the treatise answer?
options: it's on the basis of the inducing, projecting, and generating causes — all within the dominant condition
quiz.why: "It is on the basis of the inducing cause, the projecting cause, and the generating cause — all three included within the dominant condition — that dependent origination is spoken of in terms of cause." Master Cháng Bǎi: the inducing cause is the general term, covering the other two.

quiz.q: Ignorance has unsound attention as its cause; why isn't that taught first? What does the treatise answer?
options: it is only a cause preventing ignorance's severance, not a cause of defilement — and the teaching speaks of defilement's causes
quiz.why: "Unsound reasoning attention is merely a cause preventing ignorance's severance, not a cause of its defilement. … ignorance is itself defiled by nature, while unsound reasoning attention is not defiled by nature." Master Cháng Bǎi: unsound attention is the attention factor tainted by ignorance.

quiz.q: What principle determines what is listed in the twelve links, according to Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: only what is defiled is listed
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "There's a principle — only what is defiled is listed in the twelve links." Unsound attention isn't defiled by nature, so it's not listed; he adds that in the five mind-moments, attention isn't defiled until the stage of defiled-or-pure mind.

quiz.q: Meritorious and unmoving karma arise from careful discernment — why still conditioned by ignorance?
options: they arise conditioned by failing to fathom the cause of ultimate suffering
quiz.why: "Conditioned by failing to fathom the cause of conventional suffering, demeritorious karma arises; conditioned by failing to fathom the cause of ultimate suffering, meritorious and unmoving karma arise." Venerable Miào Jìng: ignorance of ripening drives demerit; ignorance of the ultimate drives merit and unmoving karma.

quiz.q: What is "ultimate suffering," per Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: worldly wealth and glory, even heavenly meditative states, are suffering — known only to the noble, not ordinary beings
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Only the noble know that worldly wealth and glory are suffering, and heavenly meditative states too; ordinary beings don't — so it's called ultimate suffering." Not seeing this, they cultivate merit and absorption for heaven. Master Cháng Bǎi: in the fourth dhyāna and formless states, beings don't regard them as suffering.
